A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAILOR research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. v1 Appendices A–E are retained as v2 Appendices B–F, with a new Additional Results appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on 12 visual manipulation tasks, including success-rate comparisons, component ablations and recovery analyses in Figures 4–9.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original residual-policy comparisons, warm-start sensitivity tests, planning-iteration and distillation results, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The default SAILOR algorithms, architectures and losses remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds an optional final post-hoc distillation into the base diffusion policy for inference without planning, extending v1's periodic expert-iteration procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 tasks from RoboMimic, RoboSuite and ManiSkill. The additional studies revisit Lift, Can and Square without introducing new datasets, task requirements or environmental conditions.

E2.justification: v2 adds a Dreamer-style actor-critic Residual Policy comparator in Figure 10 and a post-hoc Distilled DP comparator in Figure 12, both on Lift, Can and Square. The existing DP and DPPO-IRL comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The main evaluation protocol and default settings are retained. New experiments sweep warm-start fractions from 0 to 0.3 on Square with 50 demonstrations and 500,000 interactions, and test 0, 1, 3, 6 and 9 MPPI iterations on three tasks, alongside post-hoc distillation.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's training-component ablations and recovery/reward-hacking analyses. Section 4.2 and Appendix A investigate planning versus a learned residual policy, warm-start allocation, planning-iteration sensitivity, whether final distillation can replace search, and inference cost.

E5.justification: Both versions specify success-rate evaluation over 50 rollouts and report means and standard errors across three seeds. The new warm-start experiment also specifies three seeds; no changed uncertainty-estimation practice, increased run count or new significance test is reported.

E6.justification: The existing benchmark results are retained, with added results on a limited task subset. Figure 10 reports SAILOR/RP success rates of 0.99/0.85 on Lift, 0.83/0.59 on Can and 0.78/0.55 on Square. Figures 11–12 add saturation findings and show that Distilled DP approximately matches SAILOR on Lift and Can but underperforms on Square.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, search objective and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. The expanded scalability discussion offers conceptual arguments supported by existing citations, without adding formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and three stated contributions retain their central claims. The expanded closing discussion adds tentative claims that learning to search could have better data scaling with task complexity and better compute scaling than direct policy learning.

C2.justification: v2 suggests that limited diffusion-policy capacity may explain the distillation deficit on Square, attributes planning efficiency to latent-state computation, and proposes adaptive early stopping. It also expands the interpretation of data and compute scalability; the earlier recovery and robustness interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the residual policy's latent-state/base-action inputs and actor-critic training, and reports 0.014 seconds per MPPI iteration versus 0.066 seconds for base-policy action generation. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Jain et al. (2025a), Multi-turn Code Generation through Single-Step Rewards, to the LLM discussion. The DINO-WM reference receives a publication update rather than representing a new cited work. The principal positioning within local-search inverse RL remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands and renames Conclusion to Discussion, inserts Additional Results before the retained appendices, and makes localized wording and conference-footer edits. Most prose and organization remain stable. The reward-hacking paragraph introduces an incorrect reference to Figure 12 instead of Figure 8.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 10–12 and redraws Figure 8 with explicit logarithmic tick notation, legends and adjusted axis ranges. The task montage is retained as Figure 13, and the existing tables and other figures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The residual-policy comparison and Appendix A provide useful evidence for choosing test-time planning, justify hyperparameters, and clarify its cost and the limits of distillation. These strengthen the paper while retaining its main benchmark evidence. The speculative scalability discussion and incorrect figure reference are limited drawbacks that do not outweigh the empirical clarification.
